Predict a real participant’s donation in the second phase of a promotion-tournament experiment. In phase one everyone completed a twelve-question pattern quiz. In computer-graded sessions, quiz performance was graded automatically. In self-graded sessions, people privately compared their paper answers with an answer key and submitted a score that the experimenter could not verify from the answer sheet. The top half under the session’s score-ranking rule became BLUE allocators; the lower half became GREEN recipients.
The second phase is a one-shot Dictator Game: each BLUE participant is randomly paired with a GREEN participant and alone divides a fixed allocation pot. Giving d units leaves E-d units for the allocator and gives d to the recipient, where E is the current pot. Zero gives the recipient nothing; giving the whole pot leaves the allocator none of this pot. The GREEN recipient has no acceptance, veto, repayment or further choice. Neither person’s identity is disclosed, participants cannot communicate, and this allocation will not be repeated. The pot is separate from the participation fee and phase-one quiz earnings.
Use the money unit and pot specified by the user. A Canadian cent is one hundredth of a Canadian dollar; AED is the United Arab Emirates dirham. Predict the amount sent to GREEN in that unit. Output only the integer amount, without a currency name, percentage, retained amount or explanation.

Current context: a student participant in a university laboratory in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Announced fixed participation fee: 30 AED, paid separately. Phase-one quiz: up to 12 pattern-completion questions within 10 minutes. Announced quiz piece rate: 2 AED (2 United Arab Emirates dirhams) for each correct answer. Earnings will be paid privately in cash after the experiment; participants are not allowed to talk or inspect each other’s monitors.
Current task: the phase-two Dictator Game. Current role: BLUE allocator, assigned to the top half of this session’s phase-one ranking. Own allocation pot: 50 AED (50 dirhams). Current anonymous GREEN partner was assigned to the lower half. Choose how much d of this pot to send to GREEN, from zero up to all 50 AED; oneself retains 50-d and GREEN receives d. The recipient’s identity, score and demographic background are not supplied. This is the person’s first and only allocation in this experiment.
Completed own history: the phase-one quiz was automatically graded by the computer, with an integer result of 8 correct answers out of 12. The person was assigned BLUE from that session’s performance ranking; no discretionary score report was made.
Applying the announced piece rate to this integer quiz count corresponds to nominal quiz earnings of 16 AED, separate from the allocation pot and participation fee. The exact displayed or settled quiz payment is not supplied. No full session score list, numerical rank, partner’s quiz earnings, allocation result or post-experiment survey response is supplied.
Own background: age 21 years; recorded gender female. These are ordinary self-known characteristics reported in the final demographic questionnaire. The session location is supplied separately as experiment context; own nationality and the partner’s personal background are not supplied.
Predict the amount sent to GREEN in the stated unit; output only the integer.

Predict the number a real participant submits in a self-graded quiz score-reporting task. The study has two phases. In phase one the participant has ten minutes to attempt up to twelve pattern-completion questions, then compares their written answers with a supplied answer key. They are asked to enter how many questions they answered correctly. The submitted count is a whole number from 0 to 12. This count determines quiz earnings at the locally announced rate per correct answer and ranks the participant for the next phase. Participants whose submitted scores place them in the top half receive the BLUE role, described as advantageous with greater earning opportunities; the bottom half receive the GREEN role. The detailed second-phase task has not yet been explained.
The answer sheet and key are put away, and the experimenter will not inspect the person’s actual answers. The person may privately know how many they actually solved, but that privately graded total is not supplied in the prediction request. Therefore the target is the reported count the person enters, and the record does not establish whether it is accurate. Current role assignment, rank, other people’s reports and payment results are not supplied. Predict the submitted count using the provided situation and available own background. Reply with only the integer count, without explanation or extra text.

The answer sheet and key have now been put away; the person has been asked to take them home and dispose of them later. The experimenter will not inspect the answers. The actual privately graded number correct and individual answer choices are not supplied here.
The requested report is an integer from 0 to 12. The report has not yet been submitted. A higher submitted performance count improves the score used for the promotion ranking and increases the quiz earnings under the announced piece-rate rule. The top half will receive an advantageous BLUE role and the rest a GREEN role, but the detailed next-phase game, its allocation pot, final cutoff, own rank, assigned role and partner are not yet known. No other participants’ scores or later questionnaire responses are supplied.
Own background: age 21 years; recorded gender male. These are ordinary self-known characteristics reported in the final demographic questionnaire. The session location is supplied separately as experiment context; own nationality and the partner’s personal background are not supplied.
Predict the submitted score count; output only the integer.
